notes:
=== CONCEPT ===
Metasploit ipmi_dumphashes exploits the IPMI 2.0 RAKP protocol design flaw: the server sends a salted hash of the user's password before the client proves its identity. Any host can retrieve crackable hashes for any username by initiating an auth handshake.

=== RAKP FLAW ===
Design flaw (not a bug) — inherent to IPMI 2.0 spec. BMC transmits SHA1/MD5 hash during auth negotiation. Attacker receives hash → crack offline → authenticate as that user.

=== CHAINING ===
Discover IPMI on UDP 623 (nmap -sU -p 623) → msf ipmi_dumphashes → save hashes → hashcat -m 7300 → test cracked password via BMC web UI, SSH, and against all other discovered services (password reuse).

=== DEFAULT CREDS ===
Try before hash attack: Dell iDRAC root:calvin, Supermicro ADMIN:ADMIN, HP iLO uses randomized factory password (on physical tag).
